method: AI scarcity-chain overlay retained from Sep 3 and reranked on Sep 4 beneath the new refined-product/services/power-capex hierarchy. Verified company filings/releases and industry evidence distinguish contracted demand from speculative load claims and retain a supply-response clock for memory.
headlineRead: AI demand remains real across memory, packaging and optical data movement, but the Sep 4 market hierarchy gives greater immediate weight to record diesel inflation, hot Services prices/orders and official transmission/generation long-lead capex evidence. Memory economics remain exceptional while record equipment spending creates a 2028-30 oversupply risk.

newIdeas.name: SK hynix
newIdeas.theme: HBM leadership + server DRAM + advanced memory
newIdeas.thesis: SK hynix is the strongest direct HBM scarcity expression in the current stack, with HBM4 shipments, long-term customer agreements and unusually strong balance-sheet/cash-generation evidence. The valuation looks optically cheap, but current earnings contain peak-scarcity economics and should not be capitalised as a permanent margin structure.
newIdeas.catalysts: HBM4/HBM4E ramps, contracted customer demand, server DRAM pricing and continued net-cash generation.
newIdeas.risks: Memory oversupply after 2027-29 capacity additions, Samsung/Micron share gains, HBM pricing normalisation and ADR dilution/capital intensity.
newIdeas.researchNote: Highest-priority direct memory candidate; treat low forward P/E as cyclical, not structurally guaranteed.

newIdeas.name: Sandisk
newIdeas.theme: Enterprise SSD + NAND scarcity + AI storage hierarchy
newIdeas.thesis: Enterprise SSD demand is becoming a genuine AI infrastructure layer as data-centre revenue and pricing surge. Sandisk has strong balance-sheet capacity and enterprise exposure, but current gross margins and sequential revenue growth are heavily price-driven and therefore carry clear cycle-peak risk.
newIdeas.catalysts: Enterprise SSD mix, NAND pricing, AI storage demand, customer agreements and capital returns.
newIdeas.risks: NAND supply response, price normalisation, consumer weakness and gross-margin mean reversion.

newIdeas.name: Amkor Technology
newIdeas.thesis: Amkor is a lower-multiple second-order AI bottleneck with unusually high-quality demand evidence: NVIDIA is prepaying for advanced-packaging capacity and TSMC has a long-term Arizona packaging/testing agreement. This fits Power Stack's preference for named customers, deposits and funded capacity over speculative demand narratives.
newIdeas.catalysts: NVIDIA-funded capacity, TSMC Arizona ramp, AI/HPC packaging mix and utilisation.
newIdeas.risks: Packaging capacity overshoot, customer concentration, semiconductor cycle and execution on new facilities.

newIdeas.name: Coherent
newIdeas.thesis: AI data-centre connectivity is migrating from copper toward optical links as bandwidth, distance and power constraints worsen. Coherent's datacentre/communications exposure and improving leverage make it a stronger risk-adjusted optical candidate than some higher-multiple peers.
newIdeas.catalysts: 800G/1.6T optical ramps, AI datacentre mix, capacity utilisation and debt reduction.
newIdeas.risks: Optical cycle volatility, capex response, hyperscaler concentration and valuation compression.

CRDO.researchNote: Theme remains excellent, but two customers represented roughly 71% of recent revenue. Deployment timing at either customer can dominate quarterly growth; retain the concentration haircut until diversification improves.

newThemes.name: AI Memory Scarcity / Supply-Response Clock
newThemes.directionOfTravel: strengthening now / future oversupply risk rising
newThemes.summary: HBM, server DRAM and enterprise SSD remain scarce and highly profitable, but record memory-equipment spending means Power Stack must track when supply growth catches AI bit demand rather than extrapolating peak margins indefinitely.
newThemes.whyNow: HBM/server memory demand remains constrained and Services evidence indicates suppliers are reallocating capacity toward next-generation AI silicon, while future equipment/capacity spending raises later-cycle risk.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Near-term scarcity supports MU/SKHY/SNDK pricing and margins; 2028-30 capacity additions can eventually reverse the cycle if bit supply outruns workload growth.
newThemes.nextTest: Do 2027-29 capacity ramps remain absorbed by AI bit growth without material pricing deterioration?
newThemes.watchlistAction: Prefer HBM/server/enterprise exposure over consumer memory; never annualise scarcity margins as permanent.

newThemes.name: AI Advanced Packaging / Substrates
newThemes.summary: Advanced packaging remains a separate AI bottleneck as accelerators, HBM stacks and chiplets require more complex integration and customers fund capacity directly.
newThemes.whyNow: Customer prepayments and long-term agreements provide hard funded-demand evidence.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Packaging scarcity can limit accelerator/HBM shipment growth even when wafers are available.
newThemes.nextTest: Does new packaging capacity fill with contracted AI/HPC demand rather than speculative buildout?
newThemes.watchlistAction: AMKR remains a second-order scarcity play.

newThemes.name: AI Optical Migration / Silicon Photonics
newThemes.summary: Copper interconnect faces worsening bandwidth, reach and power limits as AI clusters scale, pushing more data movement toward optical links and silicon-photonics architectures.
newThemes.whyNow: Capacity ramps and customer commitments provide company-level confirmation that optical migration is moving from roadmap to booked demand.
newThemes.marketTransmission: More optical content per rack benefits lasers, transceivers, photonics wafers and related networking suppliers.
newThemes.nextTest: Do optical shipments and margins continue rising as copper reaches practical limits?
newThemes.watchlistAction: COHR remains selective priority; CRDO concentration lowers score.

ai-time-to-power-microgrids.summary: Microgrids and behind-the-meter architectures remain an important subtheme of the broader transmission/generation bottleneck, now reinforced by official ISM long-lead power-capex evidence.
ai-time-to-power-microgrids.watchlistAction: VRT remains the best current expression; require funded projects and valuation discipline.

ai-memory-wall.summary: Memory is becoming part of compute architecture through HBM4/HBM4E, tighter coupling, 3D stacking, CXL and near-memory processing. Separate this structural architecture theme from the cyclical scarcity/supply-response clock.

ai-load-quality-ghost-demand.summary: AI demand is clearly real across servers, custom silicon, memory and software, but headline requested MW remain weaker evidence than deposits, orders, backlog, customer prepayments, revenue and free cash flow.
ai-load-quality-ghost-demand.watchlistAction: Use a demand-evidence ladder: announced MW < deposits/LTAs < orders < backlog < revenue < FCF.
